Recommendation: 3-tier Panchayati Raj System 1. Gram Panchayat-Village level 2. Panchayat Samiti-Block level 3. Zila Parishad-District Panchayat Samiti level y Gram Panchayat NX
Rajasthan - 1st state
Raj at Nagaur, on 2nd October 1959 followed by Andhra Pradesh on October 11, 1959.
Ashok Mehta Committee, 1977
Proposed: 2-tier Panchayati Raj System
1. Zila Parishad (main unit)
2. Mandal Panchayat
G.V.K Rao Committee, 1985
Reviewed the working of Constitution in relation to the working of the Panchayats and Municipalities.
Proposed Zila Parishad to act as the Nodal agency for development.
L.M. Singhvi Committee, 1986
1st to recommend constitutional status for PRIs that they should constitutionally recognised, protected, and preserved.
Advocated for financial autonomy of Panchayats.
It also emphasised the importance of the Gram Sabha and called it the embodiment of direct democracy.
Nyaya Panchayats should be established for a cluster of villages.
Thungon Committee, 1988
Gadgil Committee, 1988
To examine the role of Panchayati Raj Institutions in rural development.
Members at all three levels should be directly elected.
Term should be fixed at 5 years.
Reservation for SC, ST and Women
73rd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1992
Made it mandatory to establish Panchayati Raj institutions by inserting— Part IX, Article: 243-2430
Added Schedule 11 that contains 29 functional items.
Enforced on 24th April, 1993 (that's why this day is celebrated as Panchayati Raj Day)
Then PM: P. V. Narasimha Rao.
Articles related to Panchayat
Article 243: Definition
"Gram Sabha" means a body consisting of persons registered in electoral rolls relating to a village comprised within the area of Panchayat at the village level.
Article 243A: Gram Sabha
A Gram Sabha may exercise such powers and perform such functions at village level as the Legislature of State may, by law, provide.
It is mandatory to hold at least two meetings of the Gram Sabha every year.
Article 243B: Constitution of Panchayats

There shall be constituted in every state, Panchayat at village, intermediate, and district level i.e., 1. Constitution of 3-tier Panchayati Raj System 2. Panchayat at intermediate level, not to be constituted in a state having a population, not exceeding 20 lakhs.

[Gram Panchayat] · Panchayat Samiti · Zila Parishad · Gram Gram Nyaya Sabha · Panchayat! · Panchayat Gram Nyayalayas:
Established under Gram Nyayalayas Act 2008 (effective 2nd Oct 2009)
It is a formal court (part of judicial system)
Presided over by a Nyayadhikari (judicial officer)
Has legal powers to try cases (civil + criminal)
Aim: affordable and speedy justice in rural areas
Criminal appeals are heard by the Court of Session and civil appeals by the District Court.
Nyaya Panchayat:
A traditional/local village-level body.
Established by state laws (varies from state to state)
Deals with minor civil and petty criminal disputes
Members are usually local people, not necessarily legally trained
Focus: informal justice, quick settlement Article 243C: Composition of Panchayats 1. All seats in Panchayat shall be filled by persons chosen by direct election.

2. The Chairperson of a Panchayat at village level shall be elected in such manner as the Legislature of a state may, by law, provide and at intermediate and district level through an indirect election.
Article 243D: Reservation of Seats
1. Seats are reserved for SC/ST in proportion of their population 2. 1/3rd seats are reserved for women.
Article 243E: Duration of Panchayats, etc.
1. Duration of Panchayats: A 5-year term, unless dissolved earlier by applicable laws.
2. Election Time
(a) Before the end of its 5 year term.
(b) Dissolution: If Panchayat is dissolved before its term ends, election must be held within 6 months of dissolution date. (If remaining term is less than 6 months, election is not mandatory).
3. Term of Reconstitution: Panchayat formed after early dissolution will serve only for the remainder of original term.
Example:
Po Nov 2024: Less than 6 months — (Election not mandatory)
More than 6 months > (Election not mandatory)
Dissolving power: State Government New Panchayat formed will serve remainder of the term.
(1 year in this case)
Article 243F: Disqualifications of Membership 1. Law made by State legislature can cause disqualification.
(a) A person convicted of a certain offense or declared insolvent may be disqualified from being a Panchayat member if they are disqualified by law related to state elections.
He cannot be disqualified if he is less than 25 years because minimum required age is 21 years.
(b) Disqualification is decided by such authority as determined by State Legislature.
High Court deals with the election disputes of MP/MLAs Article 243G: Power, Authority, and Responsibilities of Panchayats
State legislature, by law, endow, the Panchayat with such powers an authority that may be necessary to enable them to function as institutions of self-government.
Article 243H: Power to Impose Taxes
State legislature can authorise the Panchayat:- To levy, collect and appropriate taxes, duties, tolls, and fees, grant-in-aids, ensuring proper financial management.
Article 2431: Constitution of Finance Commission by Governor to review financial position.
Government shall lay the recommendation of Commission before the State Legislature.
Article 243]: Audit of Accounts of Panchayats Article 243K: Election to the Panchayats 1. All elections of Panchayat shall be conducted by State Election Commission.
—> The State Election Commissioner is appointed by the Governor.
2. The conditions of service and tenure of office of State Election Commissioner are determined by the Governor.
He can be removed from his office in the same manner as the judge of a High Court.
Article 243L: Application to Union Territories
Provisions of Part IX, of Constitution, which deals with Panchayats, shall apply to UT's with certain modification and exceptions.

Article 243M: Part not to Apply to Certain Areas 1. Exclusion of certain areas like tribal regions and some North-Eastem states from the Panchayat system to respect their unique governance traditions, and local customs.
However, provisions can be extended to these areas with necessary modification through specific laws.
The PESA Act, 1996:
The Panchayats (Extension to the Scheduled Areas) Act, 1996, extends these provisions of Part IX of the Indian Constitution, to the Scheduled Areas (Fifth Schedule Areas) of India.
Reservation for STs: Shall not be less than half.
All seats of chairpersons at all levels of panchayats will be reserved for STs.
Mining permissions and recommendations must be obtained from the Gram Sabha.
2. Nothing in this part shall apply to:
(a) Nagaland, Meghalaya, Mizoram (Panchayati Raj system do not exist here)
(b) Hill areas of Manipur (District Council exist here)
Delhi is the only UT where provisions of the Panchayats are not applicable.

Article 243N: Continuance of Existing laws and Panchayats Article 243N ensures a smooth transition to the new Pancha- yati Raj System by allowing all law to remain temporarily valid, while the State makes necessary changes to comply with updated constitutional framework.

Article 2430: Bar to Interference by Courts in Electoral Matters (a) Courts cannot interfere in the process of defining Panchayat constituencies, or assigning seats. oe. for Articles related to Panchayat and Municipalities:

First Municipal Corporation was set up in Madras in e 1870: Lord Mayo presented resolution of Financial Decen- tralisation
Ripon's resolution of 1882 is known as "Magna Carta of Local Self-Government'.
Municipal Corporation in Calcutta & Bombay were set up in: 1726 Ripon is also known as "Father of Local Self-Government"

There are 8 types of Urban Local Government — Municipal Corporation — Municipality — Notified Area Committee: For the administration of fast developing towns. (discontinued after 1992). Replaced by Nagar Panchayat or other Urban Local Bodies.
Cantonment Board (Military): Established under the Cantonments Act, 2006 and managed by the Ministry of Defence.
Town Area Committee: Manages small towns with limited municipal functions like street lighting and drainage.
3 Types of Municipalities
Nagar Panchayat: For a Transitional Area Municipal Council: For a small urban Area Municipal Corporation: For a larger urban Area
The municipal commissioner is responsible for implem- enting decisions made by municipal corporations, councils and standing committees.
All seats are filled through direct elections.

Article 243ZH: Interpretation Part IXB—The Co-operative Societies - (Articles 243ZH to 243ZT)
Inserted by: 97th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2011.
Grants constitutional status and protection to co-operative societies.
Provisions relating to the formation, regulation, and functioning of Co-operative societies.

The audit report of an apex co-operative society is required to be laid before the State Legislature. As per Article 243ZM of the Indian Constitution and related state laws, this mandatory presentation ensures accountability and transparency for high-tier cooperatives.
Art 243ZT: After the 97th Constitutional Amendment, a state co-operative law that is inconsistent with the amendment remains in force for 1 year.
